value.body: A counsellor helps people work through personal, emotional, academic or career concerns through structured conversation. Employers include schools, colleges, NGOs, hospitals, corporate wellness programmes and private practices. A typical day involves one-to-one sessions, keeping confidential notes, and running workshops or referring clients to other professionals.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.A./B.Sc Psychology, then an M.A./M.Sc in Psychology or Counselling

items.label: Clinical psychologist
items.note: A separate, regulated route from counselling

items.label: Work settings
items.value: Schools, colleges, NGOs, hospitals, online platforms

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree alone is rarely enough to counsel independently; most counsellors complete a master's in psychology or counselling, plus supervised practice or a certification. Freshers often start as assistant or school counsellors.

value.title: At a glance
items: Supervised practice hours matter as much as coursework.
Next roles: senior counsellor, specialised therapist, clinical psychologist (with further training).
School counsellor roles have grown with policy focus on student wellbeing.
